title: Increase your surface area for luck: ship more, meet more people, be curious and generous
summary: Theo reads and riffs on Kate Lister's article about making your own luck. His thesis: luck is a function of the number of shots on goal and the people around you. Failures compound into learning and connections, and curiosity-driven, generous interactions (not transactional asks) are what open the right doors.

principles.text: Luck is a surface area you can enlarge, not something that just happens to you; it's opportunity plus prep plus number of attempts.
principles.quote: Luck is a thing that occurs, not a thing that you have. And you can increase the surface area for your luck by thinking more carefully about what you're doing and where you spend your time.

principles.text: Build many things; the winner is rarely the one you predicted. Success comes from willingness to fail repeatedly.
principles.quote: Success doesn't come from a lot of wisdom and foresight and genius. Success comes from the willingness to try and fail over and over again.

principles.text: Failures aren't just failures: each attempt gives learning and connections, so odds improve with every run, not just via the count.
principles.quote: a failure isn't just a failure, it's a learning opportunity. So, not only does each failure increase your chance of success because of the basic statistics of running the thing over and over, every additional run by itself has an increase of the chance of success, too.

principles.text: Frequency matters enormously: a 1% shot taken twice a day hits in about two months; twice a week takes most of a year.
principles.quote: If there's a 1% chance that one of these things goes well for you, you do it twice a day, you'll get there in 2 months. If you do it twice a week, you'll probably get there within a year.

principles.text: Approach people with genuine curiosity and give before you take; don't ask for time or jobs, ask something interesting.
principles.quote: Don't ask for time. Ask something interesting and then you'll get time for free.

principles.text: Surround yourself with ambitious peers and build runway (good team, connections, savings) before betting on a startup, since you only get so many shots.
principles.quote: The people around you massively compound the lux surface area.
